evidence: "dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(full)]" and "Floyd-Warshall" show both surviving solutions optimize over all vertices while tracking only required-site masks
affordance_in_statement: No connectivity condition is imposed on sites that are not required.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this affordance: it is the defining Steiner-tree aspect of the task. If changing the task is permitted, require the selected cabling to connect all sites; otherwise explicitly acknowledge that non-required sites are usable as Steiner intermediates.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: All-pairs shortest paths followed by subset dynamic programming over the at-most-ten required terminals
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: No connectivity condition is imposed on sites that are not required.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Dreyfus-Wagner-style subset DP with Dijkstra transitions over all graph vertices
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: No connectivity condition is imposed on sites that are not required.

common_affordance: The solution may use arbitrary non-required sites as Steiner intermediates while only required sites must be mutually connected.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It applies Kruskal to build a required-site connection and does not correctly optimize the use of non-required Steiner vertices; a cheap intermediate can make the optimal solution differ from its selected spanning edges.
It uses Prim's algorithm starting from a required site, effectively constructing an ordinary spanning tree rather than solving the minimum Steiner tree for the required terminals.

recommended_edit: If a task change is acceptable, replace the non-required-site clause with a requirement that every site belong to the connected installed network; this removes the Steiner-intermediate affordance and defeats both surviving approaches. If the original Steiner problem must remain unchanged, no wording edit can defeat these exact algorithms without changing the problem.
regression_risk: Requiring all sites to be connected would make the task an ordinary MST problem and could accidentally restore the already-defeated Kruskal and Prim solutions.
